readme: THE KNOWN-WRONG BLOCKLIST. One row per (commodity, store, product) that a reasoner has ADJUDICATED wrong - the product is not the commodity, so no price for it may ever appear in that commodity's row again. audit-known-wrong.ps1 exits 2 if any listed product is priced on the board, and guards.ps1 delegates to it, so a defect that was already found and fixed cannot come back silently. This file exists because audit findings used to live as PROSE in .md files: honeydew was written up on 2026-07-29 with the store's own arithmetic and was still the published crown the next morning. Add a finding with add-known-wrong.ps1 (one command). NEVER hand-edit a name to make the gate go green - if a ruling was wrong, reverse it with add-known-wrong.ps1 -Reverse, which records who reversed it and why.
matching_key: Normalized product name, scoped to (commodity, store). The name is lower-cased, apostrophes are deleted, every other non-alphanumeric byte becomes a space, and a stranded possessive 's' is re-joined. That folds the pipeline's own corruptions together (measured over 35,362 board cells: 69 groups where several raw spellings collapse to one normal form, and all 69 were the SAME product re-encoded - Jiffy(R) three ways, 'Hy Vee' vs 'Hy-Vee', 'Clancy S' vs "Clancy's", smart quote vs mojibake pair; zero merged two different products). product_id is a SECOND, optional key used only to re-derive today's spelling of a listed product from its own store feed - it is absent at Aldi, Sam's Club and Fareway, so it can never be the primary key. Scoping to (commodity, store) is required, not cosmetic: 'Lysol Toilet Bowl Cleaner Clinging Gel' is BLOCKED as stain-remover and CORRECT as toilet-bowl-cleaner, where it is priced today; a product-global blocklist would delete a right answer.

retire_when_vocabulary.ruling-reversed: Fires when the entry carries a non-empty reversed_on AND reversed_by. This is the normal trigger for a wrong-product ruling: the product does not stop being the wrong product on its own, so the only honest way out is a named human or agent reversing the ruling on the record. add-known-wrong.ps1 -Reverse sets both fields in one command, and audit-known-wrong.ps1 stops enforcing the entry the moment they are set.
retire_when_vocabulary.commodity-retired: Fires when the entry's commodity id is no longer in commodities.json. Evaluated every run.
retire_when_vocabulary.store-retired: Fires when the entry's store name is no longer in stores.json. Evaluated every run.
retire_when_vocabulary.note: audit-known-wrong.ps1 evaluates ALL THREE predicates for EVERY entry each run and prints the ones that have fired, and it exits 2 if an entry declares a retire_when outside this list. That is deliberate: the allowlist bug found 2026-07-30 shipped two entries justified by 'the store does not carry the item' while the store carried it - a justification no machine could check, so it could never be retired and never be shown wrong.

names: Dr Teal's Foaming Bath with Pure Epsom Salt, Nourish & Protect with Coconut Oil
entries.evidence: Epsom-salt bath soap, not an edible oil. Held the coconut-oil CROWN on comparison-2026-07-28 at $5.99 / 34 fl oz = $0.1762/oz, 46% under the real cheapest. Top-of-ladder verified the whole way: real Kroger product_id, real price, working link - identity proved the price belonged to the product and said nothing about whether the product belonged to the commodity. The include rule matched on the generic word 'pure', shared with LouAna 100% Pure Coconut Oil.

Live in walmart-regular-2026-07-30 at $4.97 / 11 fl oz; a per-serving RTD beverage priced per ounce against a commodity whose real unit is dry coffee makes the coffee row unreadable. Caught before it reached a board.

names: Clancy S Parmesan Garlic Pita Chips 7.33 OZ
Clancy's Parmesan Garlic Pita Chips
entries.evidence: Pita chips with a parmesan-garlic seasoning, not parmesan cheese. Live in aldi-regular-2026-07-29 at $2.29 / 7.33 oz - about a quarter of real grated parmesan per ounce, so it wins the cheapest slot whenever it is admitted. Aldi publishes no product id, and its feed also strips the apostrophe ("Clancy S"), which is why the blocklist carries BOTH observed spellings and the normalizer re-joins the stranded possessive.

names: Idahoan Baby Reds with Roasted Garlic & Parmesan Mashed Potatoes
entries.evidence: Instant mashed potatoes with a garlic-parmesan flavour, not parmesan cheese. Held the parmesan CROWN on SIX consecutive boards, comparison-2026-07-23 through 2026-07-28, at $1.25 / 4.1 oz = $0.3049/oz. Six days of a wrong crown that nothing in the publish path could see, while Idahoan sits correctly in instant-mashed-potatoes on the same boards.

names: Blue Buffalo Wilderness Natural High Protein Dry Food for Adult Cats, Salmon, 9.5-lb Bag
entries.evidence: Dry cat food. Held the salmon CROWN on comparison-2026-07-29 at $38.98 / 9.5 lb = $4.10/lb, 20.8% under the runner-up - a near-miss with no magnitude signal, so no price band could ever have caught it. The salmon commodity already carried TEN pet-food exclude patterns and the phrase 'Dry Food for Adult Cats' walked through all ten. This entry is the reason the blocklist exists: the rule library is 43,416 excludes against 1,079 includes and still loses.

NOTE THE SCOPE: this exact product is priced CORRECTLY on comparison-2026-07-30 in the toilet-bowl-cleaner row at $4.97 / 48 fl oz - the ruling is about (product, commodity), never about the product alone, and a product-global blocklist would have deleted a right answer.

names: Pictsweet Family Size Chopped Spinach
entries.evidence: Wrong FORM. Pictsweet is a frozen-vegetable brand and this 32 oz chopped spinach is frozen, but the name carries no 'frozen' token so neither the global frozen exclude nor spinach's own 'birds eye' brand exclude could see it. It held the CROWN on fresh spinach at 0.115/oz, roughly half the real fresh crown (Aldi Little Salad Bar 8 oz 1.89 = 0.2362/oz), so the board advertised a frozen block as the cheapest fresh spinach. Brand excluded on spinach and sweet-potatoes; Pictsweet keeps its access to the frozen commodities.

names: San Marcos Traditional Recipe Crunchy Whole Jalapenos Peppers 26 Oz

It held the CROWN on fresh jalapenos at 1.3477/lb, beating six rows of actual fresh peppers (Aldi 1.70, Walmart 1.76, Baker's 1.99, Hy-Vee and Fareway 2.99). Brand excluded on the fresh jalapenos commodity only; San Marcos keeps its access to the chipotle and pickled commodities.
